correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and finite group G, the direct Brandt multiplication law proves that selected offdiagonal arcs have disjoint nonempty source and target sets; commutation of all their labels is automatic, while diagonal choices away from their endpoints are independent. Maximality forces complete source-sink fibers and maximal abelian group subgroups on each unused index. The source-target support is unique. The maximal-clique polynomial follows by multinomial counting; the complete clique polynomial follows by inclusion-exclusion forcing occupied source and target indices. The clique-number formula follows by discrete convexity. The 10-case standalone verifier builds the actual semigroup graph and compares all-clique and maximal-clique profiles independently, but the universal proof does not rely on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Kumar–Dalal–Pandey 2020 covers the same aperiodic Brandt commuting graph and proves its clique number; that result and the disjoint-source/target mechanism are acknowledged. The inspected source does not state the complete maximal-commutative-subsemigroup classification for arbitrary finite group labels, or either all-size polynomial. Margolis–Rhodes–Silva 2017 classifies ordinary subsemigroups using transitive relations, not the presently enumerated commuting-subset complex. The 2025 Rees-matrix source concerns a different product and clique-number calculations. Searches found no equivalent assertion but absence of a retrieved match does not certify novelty.
residual_risks: Published classifications of maximal commutative subsemigroups of inverse semigroups might contain an equivalent specialization not retrieved by the searches.
The aperiodic case is close to results of Kumar–Dalal–Pandey; complete enumeration and the arbitrary-group extension require explicit distinction from their maximum-size statements.
The all-clique polynomial is a finite combinatorial identity; an equivalent formulation could occur under a graph-theoretic or relation-theoretic title.
The result has not received independent literature-priority assessment.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a full structural classification of all maximal commutative subsemigroups for the infinite natural family B_n(G), and size-graded generating polynomials for both maximal commuting sets and every commuting subset. It recovers a known extremal number but goes materially beyond it by counting all inclusion-maximal objects and providing a group-data transfer principle. The abelian 3^n-2^{n+1}+2 count and the graph-equivalent but nonisomorphic C4 and Klein-four Brandt examples are concrete meaningful consequences. The result needs no separate downstream paper-sized theorem to be mathematically useful.
